page.layout: One column of running text in the middle of the page. Running head at the top centre, page number at the top right. At the foot, a gathering signature at left and a Roman numeral at right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: tutius est, etiam qui legitimæ defensionis modum non excessit, veniam seu remissionem, (vel potiùs innocentiæ litteras) commissæ cædis à Principe impetrat. Christin. vol. 4. decif. 198. Quas si quis petat, etiam eas de rigore justitiæ Princeps concedere tenetur, Faber in Cod. ad l. Corn. de Sicar. l. 9. tit. 10. def 5. In hoc tamen mores cum jure Saxonico conveniunt, quòd licet per testes occisor probaverit, se egressum non esse inculpatæ tutelæ moderamen, nihilominùs in multam fisco inferendam, & insuper in expensas & interesse amicorum occisi condemnetur.
Cùm æquius esset, eum non solùm à capitali poenâ, sed & à pecuniariâ, quæ amicis, sed & ab eâ quæ Principi debetur, absolvi debere. Faber in Cod. ad l. Corn. de Sicar. loc. alleg.

page.notes: The printed text uses "s" for long s; transcribed as plain s. The signature "R 5" is clear; "XV." at the right of the foot is read as a printed Roman numeral, placed here with the signature. The word "Princi-pe" and "Prin-ceps" keep their printed hyphens at line ends. The faint "Digitized by Google" stamp at the lower right is omitted.
